summary: Albert Debrunner was a linguist and Indologist. He held academic posts at the universities of Zurich (~1917–1918), Greifswald (~1918–1920), Jena (~1927–1935), Bern (~1935–1954), and Basel (~1940–1954).

Albert Grünwedel was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and archaeologist who studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1876–1883). He later served as Direktor at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (~1883–1921).
Albert Hoefer worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a professor at the University of Greifswald (~1840–1883) and founded the Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache in 1845.
Albert Thumb was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Freiburg (~1884–1888) and held posts at Freiburg (~1893–1909) and the University of Marburg (~1909–1910).

Albert Welter works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After earning a PhD at McMaster University (~1980–1987) under Koichi Shinohara, he held posts at the University of Winnipeg (~1995–2014) and the University of Arizona (~2014).

Albion Moonlight Butters works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Columbia University, where he earned a PhD in 2006 under Robert A. F. Thurman.

Albrecht Hanisch works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed a doctoral degree at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn and has held posts with the Nepal Research Centre and the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Albrecht Weber was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin. He spent his career at Humboldt University of Berlin (1848–1901) and the Prussian Academy of Sciences (~1857–1901).

Albrecht Wezler was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1960–1965) under Paul Thieme. He served as Director at the University of Hamburg and Director General of the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1982–2002).
Alec M. Terrana is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a BA at Pomona College by 2014, where Zhiru Ng served as a committee member.

Aleix Ruiz-Falqués specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed a PhD at the University of Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs (2016) and held posts at Shan State Buddhist University and Singapore University of Technology and Design.
Alessandro Graheli specializes in Indology and philosophy. He has held positions at the University of Vienna and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
Alex McKay works in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Indology. He earned a PhD from SOAS University of London in 1995 and held a research fellowship at University College London.

Alex Watson works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Oxford and SOAS, supervised by Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson, and held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, Harvard University, and Ashoka University.

Alex Wayman was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. After earning a PhD at UC Berkeley under Ferdinand Diederich Lessing, he held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1961–1967) and Columbia University (1966–1991).

Alexander Berzin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rutgers University (~1961–1965), Princeton University (~1965–1967), and Harvard University (~1967–1972), as well as under traditional Tibetan teachers.

Alexander Coburn Soper worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. After studying at Hamilton College and Princeton University (~1925–1944), he held posts at Bryn Mawr College (~1939–1960) and New York University (~1960–1984).

Alexander Csoma de Kőrös was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (1816–1818) and under traditional Tibetan teachers, later serving as sub-librarian at the Asiatic Society (~1837–1842).

Alexander Gardner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Michigan in 2006 under Donald S. Lopez Jr. and held a post at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.
Alexander James O'Neill is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He pursued PhD candidacy at the University of Toronto and served as a research fellow at Taisho University.
